data_status: STRICT MODE: this dataset contains only values that were compared with, or ingested directly from, retrieved sources: JPL (SSD, SBDB), NASA (NSSDC fact sheets and mission catalog, Small Spacecraft SoA report 2026, SLS page, Apollo 11 press kit, NTRS papers, ), ULA, ESA, NIST, and the Launch Library 2 aggregator. Records carry source_authority/confidence where the source is an aggregator or vendor-reported compilation. Recalled, estimated and fictional values (optimizer catalog, costs, engine/vehicle specs without a retrievable source, the user-supplied SpaceX table) are not included. Derived values are computed only from verified inputs and are labelled derived.

record.spec_note: mass/power fields are taken from the first sentence in the NASA description that states a mass in kg or a power in W; they may describe a sub-unit or a mode. Read the sentence.
record.name: Celestial Mechanics and Radio Science
record.description: This experiment used X- (8400 MHz) and S- (2113 MHz) band, on-board radio systems for whatever scientific purposes could be devised. Two primary approaches were made, one utilizing tracking information, the other taking advantage of radio trajectory variations associated with occultation of the earth-spacecraft signal. Tracking information was analyzed to determine mass and gravitational characteristics (including planetary internal composition and density estimates) of both Venus and Mercury. From anomalous characteristics observed in the X- and S-band signals during spacecraft passage through the planetary atmospheres just prior to, and subsequent to, occultation, temperature and pressure profiles were calculated. These profiles were useful to adjust atmospheric composition models. Signal cutoff provided useful information for determination of planetary radius.
